has one degree of unsaturation.

A tetraacetate with shows four OH groups in A.

Bromine water oxidises A to (one O added), which shows a CHO group oxidised to COOH; the one unsaturation is this CHO group.

HI removes all the oxygen and gives isopentane, , so the five carbons form a branched chain.

Only option (B), , has four OH groups, a CHO group and a branched skeleton; the straight-chain aldopentose (C) would give n-pentane.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

hi.content: यौगिक की से अभिक्रिया टेट्राएसीटेट देती है । का से ऑक्सीकरण एक अम्ल देता है । का से अपचयन आइसोपेन्टेन देता है । की संभावित संरचना है :
hi.explanation:
में असंतृप्ति की एक कोटि है।

के साथ टेट्राएसीटेट बनना दर्शाता है कि A में चार OH समूह हैं।

ब्रोमीन जल A को में ऑक्सीकृत करता है (एक O जुड़ता है), जो दर्शाता है कि CHO समूह COOH में ऑक्सीकृत हुआ है; असंतृप्ति की एक कोटि यही CHO समूह है।

HI सभी ऑक्सीजन हटाकर आइसोपेन्टेन, , देता है, अतः पाँच कार्बन शाखित श्रृंखला बनाते हैं।

केवल विकल्प (B), , में चार OH समूह, एक CHO समूह और शाखित कंकाल है; सीधी श्रृंखला वाला ऐल्डोपेन्टोस (C) n-पेन्टेन देगा।

अतः, सही विकल्प (B) है।

First ionization enthalpies (kJ mol−1):

3d seriesScTiVCrMnFeCoNiCuZn
IE631656650653717762758736745906

Group 2BeMgCaSrBaRa
IE899737590549503509

Assertion (A): Every 3d element (631 to 906) has a higher first ionization enthalpy than calcium (590), the group 2 metal of the same period (4th), and than the heavier group 2 metals Sr, Ba and Ra. So (A) is true.

Reason (R): Across the 3d series the added electrons go successively into the inner orbitals, which shield the outer electrons poorly. The effective nuclear charge felt by the electrons therefore increases, which is why these elements have higher ionization enthalpies than Ca. So (R) is true and is the correct explanation of (A).

Hence option A, which is the official NTA answer. (Be and Mg, from earlier periods, have higher values than some 3d elements; the assertion compares elements of the same period.)

Given below are two statements :

Statement I: Upon heating a borax bead dipped in cupric sulphate in a luminous flame, the colour of the bead becomes green

en.explanation:
In the borax bead test, a bead dipped in a copper(II) salt and heated in the oxidising (non-luminous) flame forms copper(II) metaborate, which gives the blue-green colour:

In the reducing (luminous) flame, copper(II) metaborate is reduced either to colourless copper(I) metaborate or to metallic copper, which makes the bead red and opaque:

So the bead does not become green in the luminous flame, and Statement I is false.

Copper(I) metaborate is colourless; the green colour comes from copper(II) metaborate formed in the oxidising flame, so Statement II is also false.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

en.content: The incorrect statement for the use of indicators in acid-base titration is :

options.content: Phenolphthalein is a suitable indicator for a weak acid vs strong base titration.
Methyl orange may be used for a weak acid vs weak base titration.
Methyl orange is a suitable indicator for a strong acid vs weak base titration.
Phenolphthalein may be used for a strong acid vs strong base titration.

en.explanation:
An indicator suits a titration when its colour-change range lies inside the steep pH jump at the equivalence point. Methyl orange changes colour at pH 3.1–4.4 and phenolphthalein at pH 8.3–10.

(A) Weak acid vs strong base: the equivalence point is basic and the jump lies at about pH 7–11, covering the range of phenolphthalein. The statement is correct.

(B) Weak acid vs weak base: the pH changes only gradually near the equivalence point, with no sharp jump, so no indicator, methyl orange included, gives a sharp end point. The statement is incorrect.

(C) Strong acid vs weak base: the equivalence point is acidic and the jump lies at about pH 3–7, covering the range of methyl orange. The statement is correct.

(D) Strong acid vs strong base: the jump spans about pH 3–11 around the equivalence point (pH 7), so both phenolphthalein and methyl orange change colour within it. The statement is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

en.explanation:
Microwaves are used in radar systems, which guide aircraft navigation: A IV.

Ultraviolet rays from an excimer laser reshape the cornea in LASIK eye surgery: B III.

Infrared rays are readily absorbed by body tissue and heat it, which is used in physiotherapy: C I.

High-energy X-rays destroy cancerous cells in radiotherapy: D II.

The matching is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

(Assume that the specific heat capacity of water remains constant over the temperature range of the water).
en.explanation:
The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a substance can be calculated as:

Q = m c ΔT

where Q is the heat energy required, m is the mass of the substance, c is its specific heat capacity, and ΔT is the change in temperature.

The time required to heat a substance can be calculated as :

t =

where t is the time required, and P is the power of the heating device.

The actual power output of the heating device can be calculated as:

Pactual = Pinput efficiency

where P_input is the input power to the device and efficiency is the fraction of input power that is actually converted to useful power output.

Substituting the given values:

Q = 2 kg 4200 J/kg/K (60 - 10) = 2 kg 4200 J/kg/K 50 K = 4200 50 2 J = 420,000 J

Pinput = 2000 W = 2000 J/s

Pactual = 2000 0.7 = 1400 J/s

t = = J/s = 300 s

So, the time required to heat 2 kg of water from 10°C to 60°C is approximately 300 s.
